Two side-by-side diagrams. Left diagram: A tiny point source of light, a solid black sphere, and a screen showing a single, sharp black circular shadow. Right diagram: A large extended source (a wide light bulb), a solid black sphere, and a screen showing a dark central circle surrounded by a lighter grey outer ring. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Diagram of a solar eclipse. The bright Sun on the left, the small Moon in the middle, and the Earth on the right in a straight line. Light rays from the top and bottom of the Sun touch the edges of the Moon and form a dark, narrowing cone (umbra) that reaches a tiny spot on the Earth, and a lighter diverging region (penumbra) covering a larger area of the Earth.
